summary: Match text patterns while treating a wildcard literally.
documentation: LIKE matches text against a pattern: percent represents any sequence and underscore represents one character. ESCAPE declares a single character that makes a following wildcard literal. SQLite’s default case folding covers ASCII, not all Unicode.
inputs: Text, a pattern and optionally one escape character.
returns: A pattern-match truth value; NULL input produces NULL.
caution: A plain underscore is a wildcard. Escape it when a product-code prefix actually contains an underscore.
scenarios: Find stock codes with a literal underscore separator.
Search customer names using a controlled text pattern.
Inspect export filenames sharing a documented prefix.
title: Find literal SKU prefixes
problem: From products(id INTEGER, sku TEXT), return id and sku starting with literal KIT_ using SQLite’s default LIKE behavior. The underscore must be literal, and ASCII case differences may match. Exclude NULL. Order by id.
goal: Use LIKE ... ESCAPE or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use an ESCAPE clause: pattern KIT!_% with ! as the escape character.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query using the provided tables.
SELECT 1;
